newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NORMAN STORMS TO VICTORY AT ST JUDE CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN STORMS TO VICTORY AT ST JUDE CLASSIC.

text.p: Greg Norman birdied the final three holes on Sunday to storm to a one-stroke victory over Dudley Hart in the $1.5 million St Jude Classic.
Norman used a big finish, including a 30-footer on 18, to close with a final-round five-under 66 and claim his 17th career PGA Tour victory and first of the year.

The Australian star finished 16 strokes below par with a 268 total at the rain-plagued event, overtaking Hart, who closed with consecutive 66s and was in the clubhouse with a two-stroke lead at 15-under when Norman mounted his late assault.
Norman, who has won at least one event on the Tour the last six years, picked up $270,000 for the victory, surpassing $11 million in career winnings.
Craig Parry and rookie Robert Damron, who led after three rounds, finished tied for third at 14-under 270.
Justin Leonard, Nick Price, Michael Bradley and Jay Don Blake were another stroke back.
Norman began his late charge with a birdie on 16, moving within one stroke of the lead.
On the 464-yard 17th hole, he followed a solid tee shot with a 4-iron that went 209 yards and landed close to the pin, leading to the tying birdie.

Norman used a 3-wood off the tee at 18 and left himself 190 yards from the flag. He hit a 6-iron on his approach shot that put him right of the hole from where he nailed his final birdie for a dramatic victory.
"I aimed at the 'F' in FedEx behind the green, I didn't aim at the flag," Norman said of his second shot.

"I aimed about 15 feet right of the hole and I hit the 'E' in FedEx, the first 'E,' not the second 'E.' So these are the types of things I do. I wanted to put it in the middle of the green and give myself a chance at the putt."
Norman bogeyed the first hole before rallying with birdies on two and three. He added a birdie on 13 before two pars that set up his stretch run.
Hart watched Norman from the clubhouse after a round that saw him rack up eight birdies and two bogeys. He blistered the front nine in 31 with birdies on the third, fifth, sixth and eighth holes.
As Norman closed in on the lead, Hart prepared himself for a possible playoff.
"I decided to go back out there and warm up," Hart said. "As it turns out, I could have stayed in the locker room, didn't have to work up another sweat."

For the second successive day, play had to start early so the field could finish the previous round. The leaders had completed just three holes in the third round when play was suspended by rain and lightning on Saturday.
When the third round was finally completed, Damron held a one-stroke lead over Bradley and Hulbert.

But 17 players were within five strokes of Damron with 18 holes to go, including Norman, whose third-round 69 put him just two strokes behind Damron, and Hart, who began the last round three strokes back.
